claims.text: Spin-lattice dynamics incorporating DFT and explicit longitudinal spin fluctuations can reveal a ferromagnetic ground state in a CoCrFeMnNi-based high-entropy alloy.
The ferromagnetic ground state is not captured by static DFT alone.
The initial material is a chemically disordered high-entropy alloy composed of 3d transition metals.
The alloy is paramagnetic or has fluctuating magnetic moments at elevated temperatures.
DFT should be combined with spin-lattice dynamics.
The computational method should explicitly incorporate temperature-dependent longitudinal spin fluctuations.
The relevant simulations should be performed at low temperatures approaching or below the expected Curie temperature.
Below the Curie temperature, transient spin fluctuations freeze into long-range ferromagnetic order.
Local lattice structure and chemical disorder modulate exchange interactions.
Explicit treatment of longitudinal spin fluctuations describes how magnetic moments arise and align in the disordered phase.
The longitudinal-spin-fluctuation method captures thermal excitation of magnetic moments.
Thermally excited magnetic moments eventually stabilize into a ferromagnetic configuration at low temperature.
Accounting for quantum spin effects and competition with non-magnetic configurations favors long-range magnetic order.
The ferromagnetic configuration will have lower free energy than non-ferromagnetic configurations.
The average aligned magnetic moment will increase at low temperature, indicating a stable ferromagnetic ground state.
Standard static DFT neglects longitudinal spin fluctuations.
Neglecting longitudinal spin fluctuations can cause static DFT to underestimate or miss the onset of ferromagnetism.
The findings are limited by the computational accuracy and approximations of the DFT-plus-LSF method.
Predicted magnetic moments, transition temperatures, and magnetic-state energy differences depend on model assumptions and parameterization.
The hypothesis is falsified if the method shows neither ferromagnetic free-energy lowering nor increased moment alignment below the anticipated Curie temperature relative to static DFT.
